sources.name: Your accounts at other banks
reads: Balances of your accounts at other banks
Their transactions of the last 90 days
sources.why: Your full picture: own funds for a home, idle savings elsewhere. PSD2 access ends after 90 days unless you renew it.

sources.name: eBox (government letters)
reads: Letters from the social insurance fund, tax office and pension service
Amounts and due dates in those letters
sources.why: KBC spots the social contribution regularisation letter the day it arrives and checks your reserve covers it.

sources.name: Your Peppol invoices
reads: Invoices you sent and their status (sent, opened, paid, overdue)
sources.why: Open invoices, not just payments: KBC knows who owes what before it is late.

sources.name: Company register (KBO/CBE)
reads: Your company number, start date and registered activity
sources.why: Public register: no permission needed, shown so you know KBC uses it.

sources.name: mypension.be
reads: Supplementary pension built up with employers
sources.why: An exact pension gap instead of an estimate from your income.

sources.name: Energy label database (EPC)
reads: The EPC label and score of your home's address
sources.why: The official label of your house, so the advice and the renovation obligation are exact.

sources.name: Digital meter (Fluvius)
reads: Your electricity and gas use per month
sources.why: Real consumption instead of bills: KBC measures the saving after the works in kWh, not only in euros.

step_hints.prompt: Connect mypension.be for an exact number instead of an estimate
Connect your digital meter to measure the saving in kWh
Add your official EPC label so the advice is exact
Add your savings at other banks for your real budget
Look up the house's EPC label before you order a new one
Connect eBox so KBC spots the regularisation letter the day it arrives
Connect mypension.be to see the pension you built as an employee
Connect your Peppol invoices to see open invoices, not just payments
Add your other banks so idle money there works too
